questions.stem: Why does enzyme activity decrease at very high temperatures?

options.text: The products block the active site at high temperatures
The enzyme is denatured as bonds holding its shape break, changing the active site
The enzyme runs out of energy
The substrate evaporates and can no longer bind

questions.explanation: At very high temperatures, the bonds (hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds) holding the enzyme's tertiary structure break. This changes the shape of the active site so the substrate can no longer fit, and the enzyme is denatured.
